beats.headline: Autographed and left behind
beats.text: On his way to the panel, Carl passed through a studio where an older dwarf with a CrawlCon badge, Dr. Ratchet, was preparing a demonstration at a workbench beside a quarter-sized automaton. Now the studio is empty except for a table: Automaton Table, Level 5. On it lies a regular paperback with a familiar smiling dwarf riding on the back of a mechanical horse thing, Dr. Ratchet's Guide to Building Automatons for Fun and Profit. Carl opens it to the first page. It is autographed. He takes the guide and the table into his inventory.

beats.headline: Copy out the automaton book
beats.text: Carl's question for his attorney is a legal one, and he has not heard back; Mordecai, asked first, does not know. Ask your lawyer, Mordecai says, and if he doesn't respond, wait until after the next recap episode. If they don't take it away from you, install it into the crafting studio and start working. In the meantime, transcribe everything you can from that automaton book into your scratchpad.

beats.headline: Recipes, but no parts
beats.text: Carl's level-five Automaton Table is not much use yet, despite an instruction manual filled with recipes. He has been terrified they would take the table or the recipe book back, since he basically stole them from the production facility, but so far nobody has said anything. Just in case, he has copied every recipe into his scratchpad and then into the Cookbook. The problem is supplies: he has some of the parts for several recipes and every part for none, until he finds the materials for something called Spider Stalkers.

beats.headline: A kit with the right parts
beats.text: Carl picks up a large steampunk chest, ridiculously heavy, and lifts the lid. The description comes in a different voice, like a television commercial: Doctor Ratchet's Automaton Build-It Kit, enough items for over fifteen automatons, fun for the whole family, from personal servants to flame-throwing sentinel droids. It lists dozens of parts, and Carl recognises several of them as things he needs for recipes in the instructional book he stole from the production facility. Excellent, he says.

beats.headline: What an XL box holds
beats.text: Among Carl's boxes is a platinum, dog-shaped one from Tserendolgor, holding more supplies for his automaton table, and it is an XL box, so the chest is bigger than last time. Carl knows from the automaton instruction manual that the XL boxes contain parts for a fabricator, something he has been hoping to build for a while.

beats.headline: Katia repurposes a recipe
beats.text: Katia has finished building Tran's two-part wheelchair, much like what she means to build next for Jamal, from a recipe she took out of Carl's automaton manual and repurposed. Walking around, Tran is a small mechanical crab body that can climb walls and run, for short distances, at incredible speed. Then there is the battle armour version he wears now: a second exoskeleton over the crab legs that encases him in full plate and a helmet.
